pretreatments.description: Granular sludge collection from a full-scale UASB digester of a brewery factory. Characterized by a Total Solids (TS) concentration of 15% and Volatile Solids (VS) concentration of 47%. This represents the initial inoculum for the anaerobic digestion process.
Heat shock: Boiling the granular sludge at 90 °C for 30 minutes. This treatment aims to inhibit H_2 consuming populations and enrich H_2 producing bacteria.
Aeration: Aerating the granular sludge for 24 hours using an aquarium pump with an air flow rate of 3 L/min. This treatment is intended to enrich H_2 producing bacteria.

Alkaline pre-treatment: Adjusting the pH of the granular sludge to 12.0 ± 0.1 with 3 N NaOH and maintaining it for 24 hours. This treatment is also aimed at inhibiting H_2 consuming populations and enriching H_2 producing bacteria.

Pre-treatment with WFO: Adding a saponified WFO solution (15 g/L WFO) to the granular sludge cultures (33 gVS sludge/L saponified WFO solution) and maintaining it for 24 hours. This treatment utilizes waste frying oil (WFO) as a source of LCFAs to inhibit methanogens.
Addition of 5 gVS/L FW to the pretreated cultures as well as the control cultures.
pH adjustment to 5.5 using NaOH (3 M) and HCl (3 M) after the first stage.
Addition of 5 gVS/L of untreated granular sludge to the reactors to start the second stage of AD.
pH adjustment at 7.0 since it is the optimal pH for methanogens.
